requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as the internal time source for the cluster
requirements.summary: node1's default Ubuntu pool lines were removed from /etc/chrony/chrony.conf and replaced with 'local stratum 10' and 'allow 10.100.87.0/24', chrony was restarted, and chronyc tracking showed Reference ID 7F7F0101 (self-referenced local clock) at stratum 10. chronyc clients on node1 confirmed node2 was actively polling it as an NTP client, directly demonstrating node1 is serving time internally.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to synchronize against node1 instead of a public time server
requirements.summary: node2's default pool lines were removed and replaced with only 'server 10.100.87.10 iburst' (no public pool entries remain). chronyc sources on node2 showed the source selected as current best (^*) with Reference ID 0A64570A, which resolves to 10.100.87.10 (node1), confirming node2 is actively synchronizing against node1 exclusively.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — node1 acting as an internal (local-stratum) time source and node2 synchronizing exclusively against node1 — are directly and coherently evidenced through configuration file content, chronyc tracking/sources output, and chronyc clients output. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also executed on both nodes with clear pre-restart baseline, boot-identity change, and post-restart recovery/re-sync, exceeding what the task contract required but confirming durability of the configuration across reboots.
limitations: Sync verification relied on chronyc reachability/selection state rather than a sustained clock-drift measurement over a longer window; a brief snapshot after 'iburst' may not fully demonstrate long-term stability, though the ^* selection and low offset values are strong indicators.
Backup files (chrony.conf.orig) were left on both nodes; while low-risk, their presence was not addressed by the executor and could not be independently confirmed cleaned up in later evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace is clean overall: package installs, config edits, and service restarts were all purposeful and directly tied to the two material outcomes. Two minor points: (1) cmd-6f6b02b2f48b4cf9 and cmd-0b07f8f370d64ff9 attempted to disable systemd-timesyncd on both nodes but failed harmlessly (unit already replaced by the chrony package install) — no state was changed, so this is an ineffective but non-destructive command, not a residue-causing mutation. (2) The executor left /etc/chrony/chrony.conf.orig backup files on both node1 (cmd-308bc7a1ec0044e3) and node2 (cmd-4634cd216b9f4891) that were never cleaned up; this is low-risk, bounded residue but was not restored. The independent node-restart evidence protocol (reboots cmd-a4f32d52528b464c and cmd-16fac97be5f34063) was executed one node at a time, is bounded, and is fully supported by pre/post boot-identity and chrony-health evidence, with no failed services or listening-socket anomalies in the after_executor snapshot beyond the expected chrony sockets.
